fields.features_heading: What Goes Into an Internal Comms Survey
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the survey and the results table behind it, and a follow-up prompt changes either before the next round goes out.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted for your channels

List the channels people use, from the intranet to the Monday huddle. Emergent drafts questions on where staff first hear news and what they took from it, and a prompt rewords any.
fields.feature_2:
Answers split by site and department

The survey asks for a site and a department, never a name. Results filter by either, so a plant that never opens email shows up as its own bar instead of a company average.
fields.feature_3:
A one-question rating under each update

Attach a single 1-5 rating and an optional comment to a newsletter or a CEO note. Each issue gets its own score, and the trend shows whether a shorter format lands better.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts when a group falls behind

Set a threshold on any question. When a site drops under it, the app emails that site's manager or posts in a Slack channel, with the score and the comments attached to it.
fields.feature_5:
Every round kept as rows you can compare

Each answer lands in a database you own, tagged with the survey round, the site, and the department. Put this spring next to last fall and see which groups moved, and by how much.
fields.feature_6:
Your domain, your code

Host the survey on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep the survey app as your own.

fields.usecase_heading: How Four Companies Read Their Answers
fields.tab_content_1:
For the plant floor, news comes at the shift huddle

Ridlow Foods runs three plants, and the app asked all 340 employees where they first hear company news. Of the 268 who answered, 196 work on the plant floor. Among them, 142 named the shift huddle and 9 named email. Supervisors now get a huddle script with the week's news every Monday.
fields.tab_content_2:
When the Friday update scored 2.8, it shrank to five items

Under every Friday update from Harnell Software's CEO, the app asks one question: how useful was this, from 1 to 5? Over six weeks the 12-item update averaged 2.8, and 23 comments said it ran too long. The CEO cut it to five items, and the first shorter issue scored 3.9.
fields.tab_content_3:
Which hotel staff know what changes on March 2?

Three days after Tellford Hotels announced a new scheduling tool, the app asked staff at all 4 hotels if they know what changes on March 2. If under 7 in 10 say yes, the app emails that hotel's general manager. At the airport hotel, 37 of 58 said yes, and its manager now runs a 10-minute walkthrough at each shift change.
fields.tab_content_4:
A 37-point gap between stores and head office

Twice a year, Kirwin Outdoor asks every employee to rate one statement: I hear about decisions before they affect my work. This spring, 93 of 119 people at head office agreed, against 172 of 420 in stores. Store managers now join a briefing call the day before each announcement goes out.

fields.howto_title: How to Write an Internal Comms Survey
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to write internal communications survey questions that show which messages reach which teams, then build the survey.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Pick the one thing to learn
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Use the same agree scale every round
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide what the round should settle before you write a word. Maybe it is whether frontline staff see the newsletter, or whether people trust what leaders tell them. Every question that does not serve that goal comes out.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the update, the date, or the change in the question itself. Ask whether the March 2 scheduling change is clear, not whether communication is good. A specific message gets a specific answer, and you can act on it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ten questions take a few minutes on a phone, so people finish between tasks. Save one open text box for the end and ask what they wish they had heard sooner. A longer survey loses the shift workers you most need.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Pick a five-point scale from strongly disagree to strongly agree and keep it. Changing the scale or the wording between rounds makes this spring impossible to compare with last fall, which defeats the point of asking twice.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Ask for the site, never a name
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask where people work and which group they belong to, then stop. Leave out names and employee IDs, and say so in the first line of the survey. People tell you a channel is ignored only when they know it cannot be traced back.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Reply to the results within two weeks
fields.howto_step_6_des: Share what you heard and the one change you are making, in the channel that scored best. A survey that disappears teaches staff to skip the next one. Name the owner of the change and the date it starts.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Build it and send it to one team first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe your channels, groups, and questions in one prompt. Emergent builds the survey and a database for every answer. Send it to one team as a test, fix any confusing question by prompt, then open it to the company.

faq_plan.q: What are internal communications survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Internal communications survey questions ask employees how company news reaches them and whether it makes sense once it does. A comms team uses the answers to see which channels each group relies on and which messages need a second pass.

faq_plan.q: How do I create internal communications survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Describe your channels, the groups you want to compare, and the updates you want rated to Emergent's AI survey builder. It turns that into a working survey that stores each response. Take it yourself first, reword any question by prompt, then send the link.

faq_plan.q: Which internal communications survey questions show if staff read updates?
faq_plan.a: Ask about a recent issue by name: did you read last Friday's update, and what was the main point? The second question matters more, since a correct summary shows the message landed while a yes alone shows only that the email was opened.

faq_plan.q: How often should you send internal communications survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Send the full set twice a year and a one-question rating after each recurring update. Twice a year gives a change time to show up between rounds, and the short rating catches a format problem within a few weeks instead of six months.

faq_plan.q: Should internal communications survey questions be answered anonymously?
faq_plan.a: Yes, ask where people work but never who they are. Staff are far more willing to say a manager never passes news on when the answer cannot be traced. The app Emergent builds keeps each answer in a database you own, and you decide who reads the raw rows.

faq_plan.q: How do I send internal communications survey questions to frontline staff without email?
faq_plan.a: Put the survey link where they already are: a poster with a scannable code by the time clock, the break-room screen, or a text from their supervisor. Keep it short enough to finish on a phone during a break, and ask which site they work at.

faq_plan.q: What rating scale works best for internal communications survey questions?
faq_plan.a: A five-point agree scale works best for statements such as I understand why this decision was made. Keep the same five labels in every round, and add a 1 to 5 usefulness rating for single updates, where agreement makes less sense than value.

faq_plan.q: Which internal communications survey questions test if a change was understood?
faq_plan.a: Ask one plain question a few days after the announcement: do you know what changes for you, and when? Add a free-text box for what is still unclear. The gaps people name there tell you what the next message should explain.

faq_plan.q: Should managers see their team's answers to internal communications survey questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as long as each group has at least five answers. Below that, hide the group or merge it with a neighbor, since a manager can guess who wrote what in a team of three. Share the company view next to each team's results.

faq_plan.q: Which open-ended internal communications survey questions are worth asking?
faq_plan.a: Ask two at most: what did you wish you had heard sooner, and what would you cut from the updates you get? Both point at a fix. Emergent can add a follow-up question by prompt when one answer keeps coming up.

plan.angle: The top results for internal communications survey questions are long question lists from survey vendors and comms blogs, with no way to see which channel, team or message the answers point at. This page shows four internal communications surveys built from a prompt and read by segment: a food maker learns its plant staff hear news at shift huddles, a software company rates its Friday CEO update and shortens it, a hotel group checks each property understood a scheduling change, and a retailer finds stores trail head office on hearing about decisions early. The how-to gives question design, scale, anonymity and follow-up rules, and the FAQ covers wording, length, frequency, anonymity, frontline reach and what to do with results.
